If left untreated, it can cause bleeding sores, malnutrition, emaciation and secondary bacterial infections that may eventually lead to a dog's death.

more.title: Common food preservative linked to rising suicide deaths among young people
more.summary: A widely available food-preservation chemical is emerging as a disturbing factor in rising UK suicide deaths, particularly among younger people and men. Researchers say the scale may be underestimated and are calling for urgent restrictions on access and harmful online information.

more.title: One-off campus programs fall short on preventing sexual violence, review finds
more.summary: A recent National Student Safety Survey found that one in six students attending Australian universities had been sexually harassed and one in 20 had been sexually assaulted since starting university.

more.title: A 60-year-old theory about ants, bees and wasps may be wrong
more.summary: Scientists have long thought an unusual genetic system helped ants, bees, and wasps evolve their extraordinary social colonies. A massive new analysis suggests that genetics alone can’t explain it—and the real secret may lie in other traits unique to these insects.

more.title: Nonrepeating photonic crystal may enable more tunable, reliable semiconductor lasers
more.summary: Over the past two decades, photonic-crystal surface-emitting lasers (PCSELs) have shown promise as a type of advanced semiconductor laser useful in defense- and aerospace-related applications. Typically, these devices are made with photonic crystal patterns that repeat across the area of the device.

more.title: Four more belugas arrive at Chicago aquarium from shuttered Canadian theme park
more.summary: Four more belugas have arrived at a Chicago aquarium as part of a plan to move Canada's last remaining captive whales from a shuttered theme park to aquariums in the United States and Spain.

more.title: Shackled men in 2,600-year-old Greek mass graves were likely locals, archaeologists find
more.summary: In 2016, archaeologists working at the Phaleron Burial Ground, part of the ancient Attica region, uncovered an astonishing sight: three mass graves dating to the 7th and 6th centuries BCE containing the skeletons of 79 adult men. Many were bound together with metal shackles.

more.title: Scientists simulating ant swarms find a 'first mover' can set the colony in motion
more.summary: In ant colonies, a single ant can be the catalyst for a wave of mob activity, launching brief bursts of coordinated movement involving hundreds or even thousands of swarming workers, according to new simulations from New Jersey Institute of Technology.

more.title: Scientists solve the mystery of a brain “switch” that can trigger weight loss in opposite ways
more.summary: Scientists have uncovered why two seemingly opposite ways of targeting the same brain receptor can both promote weight loss. In mice, activating the GIP receptor in the brainstem reduced appetite, while blocking it in the hypothalamus removed a kind of “brake” on fullness signals.

more.title: Hurricane poised to hit Hawaii as El Niño stirs Pacific
more.summary: A strengthening tropical storm named Lala is set to hit Hawaii's Big Island with hurricane-force gales on Saturday, bringing dangerous winds, rainfall and heavy surf.

more.title: Extreme weather is making work difficult for many people. This is what needs to change
more.summary: The UK has experienced several heat waves this summer—heat stress among workers is one of the biggest causes of weather-related sick leave. Very high temperatures can cause symptoms like heat rash and cramps, or even exhaustion and heatstroke.

more.title: Faced with historic drought, the Dutch rethink water management
more.summary: On the banks of the Waal, the Dutch branch of the Rhine, swimmers are sunning themselves on a Nijmegen beach that didn't exist before the river level dropped a few months ago.

more.title: Magnitude 7.7 earthquake strikes off coast of Indonesia and tsunami warning issued
more.summary: A powerful magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck off the coast of Indonesia early Saturday, damaging buildings and homes, and triggering a tsunami warning. Authorities urged people on affected coastlines to move to higher ground.
